- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% in 1–2 days), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment volatility.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.7 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–4% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates mean price; apply 3–7% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or bearish over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., <0.3 for 5+ days), model tends to ignore downward trends; apply 5–10% downward correction for 10+ day horizons.
